title: Parallel classification (cls) vs. autoregressive generation (ar)
question: Holding the prompt and prefix format fixed at a single input length L, how does step-by-step prediction via a learned ParallelClassificationHead (predicting o_k and flag_k in parallel) compare in sample efficiency and symbol accuracy against next-token prediction via the parameter-free SubspaceLMHead? Caveats: (1) because `x_length = L` is fixed per run, halting is a constant function of output step count in both `ar` and `cls` (variable-length halting is tested in `addition`); (2) both evaluators stop on a premature halt so post-halt steps receive zero credit, whereas at a premature halt on step k itself `cls` still emits `(pred_o[k], FLAG_FINISHED)` on separate heads while emitting `[EOS]` at step k in `ar` occupies the symbol slot.
